title: PCR Cloning with Blue/White Selection and Easy Insert Excision
author: Promega
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t89erz6

steps.title: Prepare PCR Product
steps.instruction: Verify and purify the PCR product before ligation.

substeps.instruction: Analyze an aliquot of the PCR reaction on an agarose gel to verify the desired product.
Purify the PCR product using gel-purification or the Wizard® SV Gel and PCR Clean-Up System (Cat.# A9281) to remove primer dimers and undesired products.
Minimize exposure of PCR products to shortwave ultraviolet light to avoid pyrimidine dimers.

steps.title: Set Up Ligation Reactions
steps.instruction: Perform the ligation of the PCR product into the pGEM®-T or pGEM®-T Easy Vector.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the pGEM®-T or pGEM®-T Easy Vector and Control Insert DNA tubes to collect contents.
Use 0.5ml tubes with low DNA-binding capacity (e.g., VWR Cat.# 20170-310).
Vortex the 2X Rapid Ligation Buffer vigorously before use; avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles by using single-use aliquots.
Use only the T4 DNA Ligase supplied with the system.
Mix reactions by pipetting.

steps.title: Incubate Ligation Reactions
steps.instruction: Incubate the ligation reactions to allow for vector-insert joining.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature, OR for maximum transformants, incubate overnight at 4°C.

steps.title: Prepare Selection Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare and equilibrate the agar plates.

substeps.instruction: Prepare two LB/ampicillin/IPTG/X-Gal plates for each ligation reaction, plus two plates for transformation efficiency.
Equilibrate plates to room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Transformation Tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot the ligation reactions and control DNA into sterile tubes.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the ligation reaction tubes to collect contents.
Add 2μl of each ligation reaction to a sterile (17 x 100mm) polypropylene tube (e.g., Falcon™ Cat.# 2059) or a 1.5ml microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Set up a separate tube on ice with 0.1ng uncut plasmid to determine transformation efficiency.

steps.title: Prepare Competent Cells
steps.instruction: Thaw and prepare JM109 High Efficiency Competent Cells.

substeps.instruction: Remove frozen cells from storage and place in an ice bath until thawed (approximately 5 minutes).
Mix cells by gently flicking the tube; avoid excessive pipetting.

steps.title: Transform Cells
steps.instruction: Combine the DNA and competent cells and perform heat-shock.

substeps.instruction: Carefully transfer 50μl of cells into each ligation tube (use 100μl of cells for the uncut plasmid efficiency tube).
Gently flick tubes to mix and incubate on ice for 20 minutes.
Heat-shock the cells in a water bath at exactly 42°C for 45–50 seconds without shaking.
Immediately return tubes to ice for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Recover Cells
steps.instruction: Allow the transformed cells to recover in nutrient medium.

substeps.instruction: Add 950μl room-temperature SOC medium (or LB broth) to ligation tubes and 900μl to the uncut plasmid tube.
Incubate for 1.5 hours at 37°C with shaking at approximately 150rpm.

steps.title: Plate and Incubate
steps.instruction: Plate the transformation cultures and incubate to select for inserts.

substeps.instruction: Plate 100μl of each transformation culture onto duplicate LB/ampicillin/IPTG/X-Gal plates.
For the transformation control, use a 1:10 dilution with SOC medium for plating.
Optional: To increase colony number, pellet cells at 1,000 x g for 10 minutes, resuspend in 200μl SOC medium, and plate 100μl on two plates.
Incubate plates overnight (16–24 hours) at 37°C.
Optional: Store plates at 4°C after the 37°C incubation to facilitate darker blue color development.
